dossier.mechanism: AfterShift scores every sleep, nap and coffee against the worker's NEXT scheduled shift: a forward-looking 0–100 Shift Recovery Score built from sleep quality, continuity, nap contribution and proximity to the next block. A daytime sleep and a 90-minute pre-night nap count as the recovery they are, not as a 'poor night' measured against a 9-to-5 baseline.
dossier.audienceScene: A night nurse, paramedic, firefighter, pilot or plant operator with a phone in one hand: at 07:10 walking to the car after a 12-hour night, at 03:00 in the breakroom, or searching 'night shift sleep app' at 14:00 behind blackout curtains. Tired eyes, dim or harsh fluorescent light, usually arriving on an iPhone from Google or an AI answer.
dossier.culturalHome: The rota on the breakroom wall with its D/E/N/OFF codes and a highlighter down your own row; 24-hour time and handover at 07:00/19:00; named rotations (DuPont, Pitman 2-2-3, 4-on-4-off, 12-hour, on-call); navy uniform with hi-vis and retroreflective tape; hospital and plant corridors with coloured floor lines; foil over bedroom windows; occupational-health sleep diaries.
dossier.mustProve: At a glance: this app reads your roster, not a 9-to-5. A daytime sleep and a nap show up as real recovery, and a score sits before your next shift. Next to that, the free download (official badge, plus a QR on desktop) and the honest price: 'Free — Premium from $3.99/mo, $24.99/yr, or $39.99 lifetime'.
dossier.categoryDefault: A dark navy or indigo sleep-app page with moon-and-stars imagery and a glowing ring or big sleep score. It has a split hero (headline left, iPhone right, badge row), four icon feature cards and a pricing table. This is what Calm, Rise and Sleep Cycle ship, and what the incumbent Paper & Ink template does in cream.
dossier.predictableOpposite: A bright sunrise wellness page: dawn gradient, soft pastels, serif display, a 'rest well' lifestyle tone. It is the morning-person world this audience is shut out of.
dossier.literalReading: 'After shift' read literally is the dawn after a night shift, the commute home at sunrise. The icon's metaphor is a crescent moon inside a clock face. Clock dials and dawn gradients are in the rut. Only candidate 2 (blackout room at noon) touches the after-shift moment, and it does so from inside the dark room. No candidate uses a clock face.
evidence: Front matter: price.model freemium, value 'Free — Premium from $3.99/mo, $24.99/yr, or $39.99 lifetime'; schema 0–39.99 across 4 offers; platforms [iOS]; status live; category health. 4 plans: Free, Premium Monthly, Premium Annual (highlight: true), Lifetime (one-time, Family Sharing). first_release 2026-01-01, last_updated 2026-04-03. Ratings 3.6 from 5, so no stars anywhere.

Blocks present: hero (pre_headline, headline, secondary, subheadline, cta_label 'Download Free'), quick_answer, value_points ×4, features ×6, screenshots ×6, who_for ×6, who_not_for ×3, plans ×4 + plans_footnote, privacy notes ×5, faq ×18, founder (Organization: Lagerland Apps, Finland; 4 signals; link to methodology), show_body + about_heading 'Why AfterShift exists.', alternatives_to ×5. Absent: spotlight, how_it_works (so no HowTo schema today), comparison_table, roadmap, insight_gallery, training_vocabulary, coach_cta.

App UI across 6 screens: deep navy gradient (~#0E1B2E→#132741) with translucent cards and SF Pro. Blue #3B9BE0 is primary; teal marks naps and 'Recovering'; amber marks on-call and the day-shift sun; green, orange and red dots rate caffeine. 24-hour clock ('23.00'). Tabs: Today, Coach, Roster, Sleep, Settings. Values on screen: Sleep Score 80, Shift Recovery Score 75, flexible rest window 22:10–05:40 (7.5 h), suggested nap 12:47–13:12, 6 h caffeine cutoff.
Icon: a steel-bezelled clock face with a glowing amber crescent moon on starry navy. This is the literal metaphor every direction avoids.

Transparency record (_data/transparency.yml): manifest from source; 0 tracking domains; 0 third-party SDKs; network calls 'None — HealthKit and EventKit only'; permissions Calendar (read-only) and HealthKit (read sleep); data leaves the device only to the user's own iCloud, if enabled; analytics none.

Methodology sub-page /apps/aftershift/methodology/ (a 4th sub-page that needs the Read variant): the score's four inputs are quality, continuity, nap contribution and proximity to the next shift. Nap lengths 20 / 90 / 45 min; circadian low 02:00–06:00; caffeine half-life about 5 h. This is the factual spine for every score demonstration.

Alternatives that target AfterShift: /alternatives/offshift/ (honest comparison grid, but it still says a lifetime purchase is OffShift's edge, which is stale since AfterShift added $39.99 lifetime) and /alternatives/shift-worker/. The alternatives include pairs aftershift:offshift.

Journal: 'Building a sleep app for nurses, pilots…' gives the origin (an ICU-nights friend was told she'd had a 'poor night'), names caffeine timing as the most-mentioned feature, and sends 9-to-5 sleepers to Observa. 'Not doing in 2026' rules out streaks and daily nags for AfterShift.
app_enrichment: 32 languages; recommend_why 'only shift-worker sleep app that treats naps as first-class recovery'. No AfterShift entries in testimonials.yml.

Privacy policy front matter: processes shifts, preferences (target sleep, commute, caffeine sensitivity, nap tolerance) and optional nap and caffeine logs; reads HealthKit; runs no servers of its own. The support page already has its own seo block.
Incumbent render (Observa, same template): cream ground, Newsreader headline left, phone right, badge plus 'See how it works', QR card, pill row. This is the arrangement to refuse.

candidates.name: The breakroom duty rota
candidates.why: The photocopied rota pinned by the kettle is the one document every nurse, medic, firefighter and plant operator reads each week: D/E/N/OFF codes in a grid, a highlighter down your own row, swaps written in biro. How it carries the mechanism: the roster is the only baseline AfterShift accepts. The page is that sheet plus the rows AfterShift adds under your shifts: sleep, naps, last coffee, and a highlighted Shift Recovery Score before every block.

candidates.name: The blackout bedroom at noon
candidates.family: architecture/place + lighting (the one literal 'after shift' reading)
candidates.why: Foil taped over the window, an eye mask, a blade of noon sun around the curtain: the daily ritual of every day sleeper. How it carries the mechanism: daytime sleep is the main event. The page is the dark room at 13:00, and its only light is the daylight at the curtain edge. That light falls on the day-sleep block, the nap and the hours left until the next shift.

candidates.name: The punch-clock time card
candidates.why: The manila card in the rack by the door, its IN/OUT columns stamped in violet, is the grammar of shift work even where badges have replaced it. How it carries the mechanism: AfterShift starts counting at clock-out. The page is one card where the recovery window, each sleep and each nap are stamped lines, and the Shift Recovery Score is the total before the next IN.

candidates.name: Corridor floor lines
candidates.why: Night staff find their way along coloured vinyl lines on hospital and plant floors ('follow the blue line'), often half-asleep at 03:00. How it carries the mechanism: four lines run down the page, one for each of the score's four inputs (sleep quality, continuity, nap contribution, proximity to the next shift). Each peels off to its own station, and all four meet again at the Shift Recovery Score.

candidates.name: Retroreflective tape on navy uniform
candidates.why: Paramedics, firefighters, police and plant crews work the night in navy twill trimmed with hi-vis yellow and silver retroreflective tape, made to flare in headlights. How it carries the mechanism: the rotation is drawn as a strip of tape, hi-vis for shifts and silver for sleep. When light crosses it, the naps flare exactly like core sleep: same material, same recovery.

candidates.name: Sleep diary / double-plotted actogram
candidates.why: Occupational-health clinics hand out sleep logs with one 24-hour row per day, and chronobiologists draw them as double-plotted actograms; it is the honest picture of a rotating life. How it carries the mechanism: days stack as 48-hour rows where a daytime sleep is shaded exactly like a night sleep and naps are full bars. The score sits in the margin before each shift block.

candidates.name: Night-lit flight deck / ambulance cab
candidates.why: Pilots and crews work under panels dimmed to amber to protect night vision, with labels in B612, the face Airbus commissioned for legibility to tired eyes. How it carries the mechanism: the page is lit only by light with no blue in it, the light a night worker should see before day sleep. Its readouts show the next shift, the caffeine cutoff and recovery.

styles.label: Tape & Twill

The display face, Barlow, takes its letterforms from California highway signs and licence plates.
styles.thesis: The page is cut from night-crew uniform cloth. Its one move is a strip of retroreflective tape that is the rotation itself: shifts in hi-vis, sleep and naps in silver, and both flare alike when light crosses them. It refuses the category's moon-and-glow dashboard and its split phone hero.

type.rationale: About 93 KB of latin font: Barlow Condensed 2×22 KB, Atkinson Next 3×13 KB, Mono 10 KB. Condensed caps for lettering sewn onto cloth and a legibility face for tired reading. No serif and no italic display.

styles.navigation: A deep-twill name-tape bar that does not stick. It holds the stitched AFTERSHIFT wordmark (microsite home), six in-page links in Atkinson 15px (Score, Naps, Caffeine, Rotations, Plans, FAQ) and a hi-vis 'Get it free' tab to the App Store. Under 900px the links fold into a 'Menu' button. It drops a deep-twill sheet of links in Barlow Cond 700 caps 30px, divided by 1px unlit-silver stitch lines. A 4px hi-vis bar under a label marks the current section. Focus everywhere is a 3px hi-vis outline with a 2px navy offset.
styles.signatureInteraction: Headlight Pass. Each tape band is a row of real <span> segments (shift, sleep, nap, cutoff) with text labels beneath. When a band first enters the viewport (IntersectionObserver), its silver segments switch from unlit #8F969E to lit #EEF1F3 one after another, left to right, over about 900 ms, like a passing car's lights. Naps switch exactly like core sleep. On pointer devices, hovering or focusing a segment lights it again and shows its time in a sewn tooltip. There is no glow, blur or sheen: retroreflection is a flat value change plus the bead texture brightening. No-JS: every segment renders lit and every label is printed text. Reduced motion: everything is lit on load with no sequence, and hover changes the value only.
styles.motionGrammar: One verb: light passes. Band segments step from dull to lit in sequence (900 ms per band, linear, once). The sticky tape slides up in 200 ms ease-out, and the menu sheet drops in 160 ms. Nothing fades in, nothing parallaxes, and headings never move. The screenshot row scrolls natively with scroll-snap.
styles.readModeVariant: The privacy, support and methodology pages and the OffShift and Shift Worker alternatives keep the name-tape nav and the twill ground. The masthead is a short band: the page title in Barlow Cond 800 caps 56px lit silver over one full-bleed tape seam with no timeline segments. Reading column: Atkinson Next 400, 18px/1.65, #D3D9DF on #18222F, 66ch. Comparisons become two-column ruled tables, with the AfterShift column headed by a hi-vis tab and the competitor's by deep twill. Honest trade-offs ('If you live on your Watch, this is OffShift's territory') sit in stitched deep-twill patches. Support puts the email on a lit-silver ID-tag plate with the response-time line. Methodology sets its four inputs as four tape strips. Each page ends with a slim hi-vis panel holding badge, price and a link back to /apps/aftershift/.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. Tape, twill, stitches and patches are CSS or inline SVG. It uses the icon, the six screenshots, the QR and the OG card, all of which exist.
styles.risk: Navy with fluorescent yellow sits close to the 'dark + one neon accent' rut and to emergency-service livery. It holds only if the yellow stays flat fabric (panels and tape) and never becomes glowing lines, and if no Battenburg checks, insignia or service words (PARAMEDIC, FIRE) appear. Nurses and pilots don't wear reflective tape, so the world speaks most directly to medics, fire and plant crews. Large hi-vis areas are bright for someone heading to day sleep, so yellow must stay under about 12% of any viewport.
styles.memoryTest: The sleep-app page made of uniform cloth: a strip of reflective tape ran across it, and when the light passed, the naps lit up exactly like the main sleep.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

allpaid-a keeps Barlow, the free DIN stand-in that is native to a German-language Abfahrt poster. aftershift-a sets its uniform back-lettering in Mohave 600/700, a caps-first condensed sans that is unused elsewhere, and keeps Atkinson for text.

aftershift-a keeps navy and Atkinson: the uniform colour and the low-acuity argument are literal. observa-a takes its icon's own warm night (~#15110F), with apricot as the only colour and no glow. Constellation names and labels move into one sans with tabular figures (e.g. League Spartan, from the Futura lineage of star charts), with no mono and no spaced Didone caps. Keep Bodoni Moda for the H1 at most.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

Keep it on allpaid-a, where the yellow departures poster is a DIN-model sign and Barlow is the closest open DIN relative. Move aftershift-a's back-lettering to Mohave 700 (about 9 KB, caps). Mohave stops at 700, so the 800 weight becomes 700.

styles.label: The Breakroom Rota
styles.lineage: The ward or station duty rota. An A3 sheet typed in a utilitarian grotesk, run off the office photocopier and pinned to the breakroom corkboard. It has an admin header (period, issued, approved), a grid of staff by days filled with D/E/N/LD/OFF codes, a key of codes and notes at the foot, plus a highlighter stripe along your own row and biro amendments. Related: the named crew-rotation charts (DuPont, Pitman 2-2-3).
styles.thesis: The page is the rota sheet plus the rows AfterShift adds under your shifts: sleep, naps, last coffee, and a highlighted Shift Recovery Score before every block. The worker's own schedule is visibly the baseline. It refuses the category's moon-and-score dashboard and its phone-on-the-right hero.
styles.scene: A nurse or medic at 18:40 before night handover, reading the new rota pinned to the breakroom corkboard under a cool fluorescent tube → light, single scheme (color-scheme: light).

styles.lineage: Hospital and plant wayfinding: coloured vinyl floor lines that peel off at junctions ('follow the blue line'), dark hanging sign blades with reversed text and arrow pictograms, and white enamel directory plaques. styles.thesis: Four floor lines, one for each of the Shift Recovery Score's four inputs, run the length of the page. Each peels off to its own station, and all four meet again at the score, so the method is something you walk rather than read. It refuses the category's stacked feature cards and phone-on-the-right hero.

styles.signatureInteraction: Follow the Line. Each section has real tape elements: a vertical bundle in a left gutter (desktop x200–420, mobile x16–52). At each station, one tape turns 90° with a mitred corner and runs under that station's sign blade. Tape segments draw downward at walking pace as you scroll, using a CSS scroll-driven animation (animation-timeline: view(), scaleY 0→1) with an IntersectionObserver class as fallback. Hovering or focusing a station label dims the other three tapes to 30%, so one input's route reads on its own. No-JS: every tape is fully drawn. Reduced motion: tapes are drawn with no scroll link, and hover only dims.
styles.motionGrammar: Lines advance with the walker: tapes draw with scroll position, never on a timer. Sign blades and text never move. The Directory blade drops in 160 ms, the sticky blade slides in 200 ms, and FAQ arrows turn 90° in 120 ms.

styles.risk: Wayfinding signage can read as a real hospital. It must avoid NHS-like blue and Frutiger, any real hospital pictogram set, and the green running-man exit sign. Nurses will recognise it at once; pilots and fire crews see it less. The tape bundle's geometry across breakpoints is the hardest build of the three. At 390px the 36px gutter narrows the reading column to about 318px. Four saturated colours can tip into a children's map if the lino and blades don't hold them down.

canon: A dark navy sleep-app page: split hero with the headline left and an iPhone showing the 75 Shift Recovery Score on the right, an App Store badge and QR row, four icon feature cards (naps, rotations, caffeine, privacy), a pricing table and an FAQ accordion. The category standard played straight.
notes: Degraded roll: the roll service was offline, so there were no catalog challengers; the network was not retried, as instructed. Seed key bd9034af, assigned index 5; re-roll 1 gave index 4 (distinct on the first try, so no further re-rolls). A = candidate 5 (THE ROLL), B = candidate 1 (IMPECCABLE’S PICK, my top-ranked), C = candidate 4 (SECOND ROLL). The three differ in world (uniform cloth / paper rota / corridor floor), topology (horizontal tape bands / stacked document sheets around a data grid / one vertical route with stations) and light (dark Committed / light Restrained / light Full palette). Every face was verified on Fontsource with npm view and npm pack: barlow-condensed, atkinson-hyperlegible-next, atkinson-hyperlegible-mono, archivo (variable wdth+wght via @fontsource-variable/archivo), reenie-beanie, signika, signika-negative. Each style stays at or under 120 KB of latin font. Findings for the build: (1) /apps/aftershift/methodology/ is a fourth sub-page and needs the Read variant too. (2) /alternatives/offshift/ still calls a lifetime purchase 'OffShift's edge' even though AfterShift now sells $39.99 lifetime; the copy needs a fix. (3) The incumbent sticky bar prints 'Free · Pro optional' for freemium, but AfterShift's tier is called Premium. (4) The alt text for screenshot 1 says 72/100, while the real screens show a Shift Recovery Score of 75 and a Sleep Score of 80, and screenshot order does not match the captions (2 = recovery window and scores, 3 = plan and nap, 4 = caffeine, 5 = trends, 6 = roster). Every illustrative figure in the styles uses the values on the real screens and is labelled illustrative. (5) There is no how_it_works block, so no HowTo schema is emitted. The methodology's four inputs are the natural source if the owner wants one; that is a content task. (6) Ratings count is 5, so no stars appear anywhere.

pageFixes.issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
